classification.difficultyReason: Combines tangent geometry, cosine and arc length, including reversing the calculation to find a lighthouse height.

content.prompt: **Distance to the horizon.** A lighthouse has a height of $d$ metres above sea level. The radius of the Earth is $r=6371$ kilometres. We are interested in measuring the length $l$ of the arc from the base of the lighthouse to a point on the horizon. In the formulas below, express $r$ and $d$ in the same units and measure $\theta$ in degrees.

spec.description: Earth cross-section with vertical lighthouse height segment, tangent to an upper-right horizon point, two radii, a derived right-angle marker and highlighted surface arc. The decorative lighthouse is replaced by its height segment.
spec.mathematics: The horizon radius is perpendicular to the sightline. The vertical centre-to-top distance is r+d; the central angle is theta and the intervening surface arc has length l. Diagram is schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and geometric relationships are visible.

answer.worked:
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the horizon, so the triangle is right-angled. With $r$ and $d$ expressed in the same units,
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{r}{r+d}.\end{align*}$$

answer.short: The arc is $\dfrac{\theta}{360}$ of the circumference $2\pi r$, where $\theta$ is measured in degrees.
answer.worked:
An angle of $\theta$ degrees describes $\dfrac{\theta}{360}$ of a full revolution. The arc is the same fraction of the circumference:
$$l=\frac{\theta}{360}\times2\pi r.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Given the lighthouse is $d=20$ metres tall, find the length $l$ of the arc to the nearest kilometre.

answer.short:
$16\text{ km}$.

Convert the height to kilometres, find $\theta$ using cosine, then calculate the arc length.
answer.worked:
Use $d=0.020\text{ km}$ and evaluate the inverse cosine in degrees. Keep the angle unrounded in the arc calculation.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{6371}{6371+0.020}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{6371}{6371.020}\right)\\l&=\frac{\cos^{-1}(6371/6371.020)}{360}\times2\pi\times6371\\l&\approx15.96368796\text{ km}\\l&\approx16\text{ km}\quad\text{(nearest kilometre).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Given the arc length to the horizon is $l=20\text{ km}$, find the height $d$ of the lighthouse to the nearest metre.

answer.short:
$31\text{ m}$.

Find the central angle from the arc length, then rearrange the cosine relation.
answer.worked:
Use kilometres throughout the calculation and evaluate cosine in degrees.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\frac{20\times360}{2\pi\times6371}\\6371+d&=\frac{6371}{\cos\theta}\\d&=\frac{6371}{\cos\theta}-6371\\d&\approx0.03139237502\text{ km}\\d&\approx31.39237502\text{ m}\\d&\approx31\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre).}\end{align*}$$
